question_snapshot.stem_en: Which decision is associated with the earlier narrow interpretation of Article 21 that was subsequently displaced by the broader approach discussed in Maneka Gandhi?
Which pair correctly gives the years of A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras and Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India, respectively?
Which governmental action was directly challenged in Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)?
options_en: Refusal to issue her first passport
Impounding her existing passport under Section 10(3)(c) of the Passports Act
Cancellation of her passport through a criminal conviction

A law authorises detention through a procedure that is arbitrary and fundamentally unfair. Officials argue that enactment by the legislature alone satisfies Article 21. Which is the best response after Maneka Gandhi (1978)?
options_en: Any enacted procedure necessarily satisfies Article 21.
Only executive action, never legislation, can be tested under Article 21.
Fairness matters only if the person is a citizen.
The procedure must also be fair, just and reasonable.

question_snapshot.stem_en:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court has read the right to food into Article 21’s protection of life with dignity.
2. This means that the NFSA’s targeted foodgrain entitlement automatically applies identically to every household, without regard to its eligibility provisions.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

A person claims that the right to sleep permits occupation of any public premises regardless of reasonable time, place and manner rules. Which response reflects the sleep discussion in Ramlila Maidan (2012)?
options_en: Sleep removes every restriction on location.
Sleep has no connection with life or liberty.
Protection from unlawful disruption of sleep does not exclude reasonable time, place and manner regulation.
Permission for a public meeting necessarily includes unrestricted overnight occupation of the venue.

question_snapshot.stem_en:
Consider the following statements about the right to reputation:
1. The Supreme Court has recognised it as a component of Article 21, to be balanced with freedom of speech.
2. This recognition makes every adverse criticism of another person automatically punishable, without examining the applicable law.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
A homeless person dies and the body is unclaimed. An authority argues that constitutional dignity has no relevance to the treatment of the body because life has ended. Which assessment is correct?
options_en: The argument is correct because an unclaimed body is outside every constitutional protection.
Respectful treatment after death is relevant only if the deceased owned property.
Dignity and fair treatment extend to the body after death; being unclaimed does not justify indignity.
The Constitution requires any requested funeral practice to prevail over every lawful public-health restriction.

question_snapshot.stem_en: An organiser claims that freedom of speech gives an unrestricted right to use amplifiers at obnoxious levels, forcing unwilling neighbours to listen. Which assessment accords with the Supreme Court’s noise-pollution ruling?
options_en: Amplified speech is exempt from every constitutional limit.
Article 19(1)(a) permits the organiser to override neighbours’ Article 21 interests.
Permission to hold the event necessarily dispenses with all applicable noise limits.
Freedom of expression does not authorise such forced exposure; Article 21 protects a peaceful life against harmful noise.

What was the scope of the Supreme Court’s 2018 holding in Navtej Singh Johar concerning Section 377 IPC?
options_en: It made all sexual conduct lawful regardless of consent.

It invalidated Section 377 in its entirety for every category of conduct.
